objectives.title: Tell Eurylochus You Will Climb
objectives.hint: He is still at the fire, watching the smoke on the mountain. Give him the word to lead on.

happening.text: The party leaves the beach camp for the smoke on the mountain, and Elpenor is left holding the fire alone.

npc/antiphos.doing: Sitting the fire out with his knees drawn up, sizing the mountain and saying nothing about it.

npc/elpenor.doing: Feeding the driftwood fire too fast and talking to keep the dark off his back.

npc/eurylochus.doing: Working the crew count in his head at the class-post and arguing the smoke to the captain's face before the order comes.

obj/climb-out.text: Eurylochus shoulders a coil of rope and starts up the worn path. Follow the smoke.

on_complete.text: Antiphos hoists the wine and the meal-sacks onto one shoulder. "Somebody carries the man's dinner," he says, and falls in behind you. Elpenor stays with the fire — alone, and burning it high.

on_arrive.text: Antiphos sets the sacks down in the light of the mouth and stays there, catching his wind and counting lambs.

happening.text: Antiphos carries the provision-sacks up the switchbacks and sets them down in the light of the cave mouth.

happening.text: The sea puts what is left of the crew on an unknown shore, with one fire above the tideline and one thread of smoke on the mountain.

objectives.title: Follow Eurylochus to the Cave
objectives.hint: Climb up off the sand behind him: through the grazing meadow, past the low stone sheep-fold standing walled and empty, and up the switchbacks of the mountain's face to the smoking cave mouth where the great boulder rests.

happening.text: The party reaches the cave mouth and looks into a hall somebody keeps.
happening.subject: anchor/mouth

npc/antiphos.doing: Setting the provision-sacks down in the light of the mouth, catching his wind and counting the pens off on one finger.

happening.text: The party climbs the mountain face and reaches the mouth of the cave the smoke comes from.

objectives.title: Step Into the Cave
objectives.hint: Move in past the mouth to the first broad shelf of the hall, where the racks begin.

happening.text: The party crosses into the hall proper and the way back out is a long walk behind them.
happening.subject: anchor/checkpoint-1

objectives.title: Take a Wheel of Cheese
objectives.hint: The cheese is racked on the shelves by the entry. Take a wheel from the barrel among them.

happening.text: Odysseus takes a wheel of kefalotyri from the barrel among the racks.
happening.subject: item/kefalotyri-cheese

objectives.title: Decide With Eurylochus
objectives.hint: He is at your shoulder by the cheese racks. Tell him whether you run for the ship or wait for the owner of this cave.

happening.text: The crew put the argument to the captain — take the food and go, or stay and meet the host — and he answers it.

obj/checkpoint.text: Cheese racked to the roof, lambs penned and sorted by age, the milk pails still warm on the shelf. Whoever keeps this house walked out of it this morning meaning to walk back in tonight.

obj/blind.text: The hills answer him. His own kind call in at the stone: "Polyphemus! Who is killing you?" And he roars his ruined face against the rock: "NOBODY! Nobody is killing me!" A pause. Then, going away up the mountain: "If nobody hurts you, it is a sickness from Zeus. Pray to your father." And the footsteps do not come back. He hears them go.

The hills answer him. His own kind call in: "Polyphemus! Who has done this?" And he roars back the name you laid down over the wine, whole and proud: "ODYSSEUS! Sacker of cities, son of Laertes, of Ithaca — he was under my roof!" And they believe him. "Hold, cousin — we cannot shift your stone from without. Wait for the light; at dawn every hand on the mountain opens it together." Perimedes has your sleeve: "They come back at dawn, Captain. We leave before they do."

The hills answer him. His own kind call in: "Polyphemus! Who has done this?" And he roars back the name you gave him over the wine: "AITHON! A Cretan, out of Crete — at my own fire!" A silence. Then, cool and turning away: "A Cretan. Cousin, the Cretans lie; it is the one thing known of them. Sleep it off." And the footsteps go, half-convinced of nothing, and do not come back tonight.

effects.text: Salt air, and no light in it at all. Somewhere under the noise a very old voice is being told what was done to its son, and the water starts to come in wrong.

happening.text: The shore at the mountain's foot gives up its dead into the storm.
happening.subject: wave/storm-shore

effects.text: Do not stop to fight them. Nothing on this island is worth one more man. Get down the mountain and get to the oars.

happening.text: Drowned wade out of the surf at the dead camp fire, between the mountain and the ship.
happening.subject: wave/storm-fire

happening.text: The flock is let out to graze at first light, and the crew go out under them.
happening.subject: anchor/boulder

objectives.title: Down to the Ship
objectives.hint: Come down off the mountain to the strand where the galley rides at her gangplank, oars manned and waiting.

happening.text: The party crosses the last of the sand to the waiting galley.
happening.subject: anchor/gangplank

objectives.title: Board and Give Way
objectives.hint: Cross the gangplank to the deck and take your place. However you leave him, the water is listening.

happening.text: Odysseus goes up the gangplank and the oars take the ship off the beach.

npc/antiphos.doing: Back at the strand with the sacks aboard and every man he climbed with still on his feet.

barks: Sacks are aboard, Captain. Everything we came in with, and one wheel to the good.
Say the word and I will shove her off. I would like very much to be rowing.

npc/elpenor.doing: Standing over a fire he kept all night, counting the party back down the path and asking the one question nobody wants to answer.
Standing over the fire he kept, with a speech prepared for a loss that never happened.

npc/eurylochus.doing: At the gangplank counting heads out loud for the third time and refusing to grieve until the oars are moving.
At the gangplank counting the party aboard twice over, on the one branch of this island where the number comes out whole.

npc/perimedes.doing: On the sand with two fists of ram's wool still in them, laughing wrong and asking to be told the count is four.
Down on the sand ahead of everyone with the wine-skin still unopened, working out whether the giant counts his cheeses.

obj/last-sand.text: Behind you, high on the mountain, the blind giant has not gone back inside. He has set himself across the mouth of his own cave with his hands out and his head turned, waiting for a sound to hate. Whatever is still in there is his now.
The gangplank is ten strides off, and the sea grudges you every one of them: the shallows give up their dead at your back.

happening.text: A last surge of drowned rises between the party and the plank.
happening.subject: wave/storm-surf

obj/board-nobody.text: Oars out, and the strand slides away astern. Nobody looks back at the mountain; there is a great deal of open water to be got between you and it before anyone feels like talking.

happening.text: The survivors come down the mountain to the boat, with the blinded giant holding the mouth behind them.

obj/aboard.text: Open water on every side, and the oars finding their stroke. Somewhere behind the dark the island is still there, and it is already somebody else's problem.

effects.text: NOBODY

You won the cave. He will tell the story to the end of his days and never once get the name right, and the neighbours who came as far as the stone have gone back to their own fires believing a sickness took him. No song, no herald, no one ashore who will ever hear it. You will live on that. You will have to.

You won the cave, and then you signed it. Somewhere astern the mountain is awake — hands on the slope, cousin calling to cousin, every one of them coming at first light to lift the stone off a man who can now give the sea your name and your father's. Eurylochus has the stroke going and will not look back. Whatever you bought in there, the water will come to collect.

You won the cave, and a Cretan took the credit. The hills heard the name, weighed it and went back to sleep — a trader out of Crete, and Cretans lie, so nothing worth waking for was said at all. No one is coming for Aithon; there was never an Aithon to come for. You have your crew, your water and a clean horizon, and the best hour of your life belongs to a man who does not exist.

happening.text: NOBODY: the crew that is left rows away from an island whose keeper cannot name them.
Open water, and the island falls away astern with the story of it already fixed.

effects.text: THE QUIET SAIL
Ithaca inside the month. Safe, and fed, and a little smaller for it — and every man you came in with still at his oar.

happening.text: THE QUIET SAIL: every man who came ashore leaves it, and no story is made of any of them.
The quiet sail: a whole crew, a full hold, and a story nobody aboard will ever tell twice.

effects.text: You set your shoulder to the great stone. It does not so much as grind. No blade you carry will bite it — whatever opens this cave, it will not be you.
He Wakes
Never strike a sleeping god's son. He comes up off the floor with his whole strength, and there is nothing in this cave that can stand against that.

happening.text: The giant who could be talked to is gone the moment he is struck.
happening.subject: npc/polyphemus

happening.text: Polyphemus comes awake as something that only fights.
happening.subject: actor/polyphemus-roused

happening.text: The roused giant comes for whoever woke him, and the starting kit does not beat him.
happening.subject: actor/polyphemus-roused

effects.text: Your blade turns on his hide like a stick on a ship's keel. He sets down the pail. Slowly. In his own house, under his own stone, you have raised a hand to him — and he rises to answer it in full.

happening.text: The host stops being a host the moment a blade is put in him.
happening.subject: npc/polyphemus

happening.text: Polyphemus answers the strike in kind.
happening.subject: actor/polyphemus-roused

happening.text: The roused giant comes for the man who struck him, in a house with the stone across it.
happening.subject: actor/polyphemus-roused

effects.text: He Is Still There
Your foot turns a pebble in the mouth of the cave and his head comes round on the sound like a door slamming. He told the hills he would eat you last. He did not say he had stopped.

happening.text: The blinded giant is still across his own mouth, and anything that comes back in is his.
happening.subject: actor/polyphemus-walker
